a: The disjointed letters at the beginnings of surahs are generally among the ambiguous matters whose true meaning only Allah knows; in them is an indication of the inimitability of the Qur’an: it is composed of the very letters of which the Arabs’ language consists. The Arabs’ inability to produce its like — though they were the most eloquent of people — shows that the Qur’an is revelation from Allah. Opinions on interpreting these letters are many and varied. They comprise fourteen letters of the Arabic alphabet and form the phrase: “A wise text with a decisive secret”; a group of interpreters said they are Allah’s secret in the Qur’an.

Muhammad (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): the unlettered Arab Prophet, of Banū Hāshim. He was born in Makkah a few months after the death of his father, Abdullah. His mother, Āminah, died while he was still a child. His grandfather, Abd al-Muṭṭalib, cared for him, then his uncle, Abū Ṭālib. He tended sheep for a time. He married Lady Khadījah, daughter of Khuwaylid, when he was twenty-five years old. He called people to Islam, meaning faith in the One Allah and His Messenger. He began his call in Makkah, whose people persecuted him, so he migrated to Madinah, where a number of the Anṣār gathered around him in the year six hundred and twenty-two CE; that year became the beginning of the Hijri calendar. He is one whose praiseworthy qualities are numerous, the seal of the prophets and the noblest of the messengers. Allah revealed to him the Noble Quran containing the teachings of Islam, which Allah chose as a religion for humanity. Its monotheism and legislation made it a universal religion encompassing every aspect of life and suitable for all people in every time and place. Thus his message, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was to all people. Thanks to the merits it contains, Islam spread to all parts of the earth. He died after performing the Farewell Pilgrimage.
